page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2055.0 and demonstrated strong capabilities in single-threaded gzip compression at 33.32 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.87 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory performance metrics generally fall within the average tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 12373.16 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7957.0. However, memory performance is a relative bottleneck, as evidenced by a weak Passmark memory score of 1782.21 and a medium model LLM text generation speed of 7.8 tokens/sec.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile and dedicated CPU allocation, the c7i-flex.2xlarge is structured for workloads requiring consistent processing power without massive memory footprints. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) makes it suitable for vector calculations, cryptography, and light machine learning inference. It is well-suited for tasks such as single-threaded data compression, software compilation, and web serving, though workloads requiring high memory bandwidth or local storage will face limitations.
